subject.title: [Bug/Docs]: local+hybrid memory_search quality can appear unstable due to extraPaths path drift + benchmark-file contamination

question: Should OpenClaw add a public memorySearch exclusion and path-hygiene contract now, and what scope should it cover across builtin indexing, QMD, status diagnostics, and docs?
rationale: The request is not a narrow bug repair because it adds public config and changes which files enter the recall corpus, while repository policy treats memory/session-state and config/default surfaces as compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Repair narrow builtin exclusion first
options.body: Repair and land the open excludePaths PR with merged defaults, index-identity coverage, and explicit builtin-only documentation while tracking QMD and diagnostic parity separately.

options.title: Require one cross-backend contract
options.body: Pause the open PR until builtin, QMD, watcher behavior, docs, and status diagnostics share one exclusion/path-hygiene model.

options.title: Docs and diagnostics only
options.body: Defer public exclusion config and improve memory status/docs guidance around path drift, broad extraPaths, and benchmark contamination.

recommendation.title: Repair narrow builtin exclusion first
recommendation.body: Repair and land the open excludePaths PR with merged defaults, index-identity coverage, and explicit builtin-only documentation while tracking QMD and diagnostic parity separately.

likelyOwner.reason: The current memory-host SDK and memory-core manager history makes this the best available owner for the config/runtime boundary decision.
